cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What is the exact sequence of steps from running `use schoolDB` to materializing `schoolDB` on physical disk?
cards.back:
1. `use schoolDB` binds the active session pointer in memory.
2. `db.students.insertOne({ name: "Aditi", age: 18 })` auto-creates `students` and materializes `schoolDB` on disk.
cards.key_takeaway: Switching context via use is an in-memory pointer update; disk materialization happens on first write.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    S1["1. Run use schoolDB"] --> S2["2. Bind Session Pointer in Memory"]
    S2["2. Bind Session Pointer in Memory"] --> S3["3. Run db.students.insertOne(...)"]
    S3["3. Run db.students.insertOne(...)"] --> S4["4. Materialize schoolDB on Disk"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Context Switching & Creation (use <databaseName>)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the Database Catalog Inspection diagram, how does the storage catalog filter unwritten databases when `show dbs` runs?
cards.back: The catalog inspects physical disk extents and excludes any session-selected database that has zero written collections, while listing `admin`, `config`, `local`, and populated user databases.
cards.key_takeaway: The show dbs command filters out any in-memory database context that has zero allocated bytes on disk.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Execute show dbs"] --> B["Inspect Physical Storage Catalog"]
    B["Inspect Physical Storage Catalog"] --> C["Display Populated DBs (admin, config, local, schoolDB)"]
    B["Inspect Physical Storage Catalog"] --> D["Omit Unwritten In-Memory Contexts"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Catalog Inspection (show dbs)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the database deletion process, why must `use <databaseName>` precede `db.dropDatabase()`?
cards.back: Because `db.dropDatabase()` accepts zero arguments and targets whatever namespace is currently bound to the `db` pointer, verifying context with `use schoolDB` prevents accidental deletion of the wrong database.
cards.key_takeaway: Because db.dropDatabase targets the active session context without arguments, always verify your current database first.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Step 1: Verify Context with use schoolDB"] --> B["Step 2: Invoke Zero-Arg db.dropDatabase()"]
    B["Step 2: Invoke Zero-Arg db.dropDatabase()"] --> C["Step 3: Unlink All Collections and Documents"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Destruction & Removal (db.dropDatabase())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does explicit `db.createCollection(name, options)` differ from implicit auto-creation in terms of schema governance?
cards.back: Implicit creation uses default settings, whereas `db.createCollection(name, options)` configures JSON Schema validators or capped ring buffers.
cards.key_takeaway: Explicit db.createCollection is required when configuring validation rules or capped ring-buffer collections.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Schema Governance Options"] --> A["Implicit Insert: Default collection settings only"]
    D["Schema Governance Options"] --> B["Explicit createCollection: Custom validators & capped size"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 2. Collection Architecture & Structural Management > Collection Creation Mechanics (db.createCollection())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: Under what exact conditions does a collection namespace register in the output of `show collections`?
cards.back: A collection appears in `show collections` only after explicit creation via `db.createCollection("students")` or after at least one document is inserted via `insertOne()` or `insertMany()`.
cards.key_takeaway: Collections appear in show collections only after explicit creation or initial document insertion.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
mindmap
  root(("Collection Visibility Rules"))
    "Active DB selected via use"
    "Explicit db.createCollection()"
    "Implicit first insertOne / insertMany"
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 2. Collection Architecture & Structural Management > Collection Inventory Inspection (show collections)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What overall architectural concept does the Collection Removal Mechanics (`db.<collection>.drop()`) diagram illustrate?
cards.back: The diagram illustrates simultaneous three-part destruction: removing the `students` collection container, purging all BSON documents, and deallocating all primary (`_id`) and secondary B-tree indexes.
cards.key_takeaway: Dropping a collection deletes all documents and deallocates every index defined on that collection.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["db.students.drop() Command"] --> B["1. Remove Collection Namespace"]
    A["db.students.drop() Command"] --> C["2. Purge All Stored BSON Documents"]
    A["db.students.drop() Command"] --> D["3. Deallocate All B-Tree Indexes"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 2. Collection Architecture & Structural Management > Collection Removal & Destruction (db.<collection>.drop())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: During `db.students.insertOne(document)`, what automatic steps does MongoDB perform before persisting BSON to disk?
cards.back: When `db.students.insertOne({ name: "Rahul", grade: 9, subjects: ["Math", "Science"] })` runs, MongoDB auto-creates `students` if missing, generates a unique 12-byte `ObjectId` for `_id` if omitted, and serializes the fields into BSON.
cards.key_takeaway: The insertOne method auto-initializes missing collections and assigns a unique _id ObjectId automatically.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Step 1: Receive Single Document Object"] --> B["Step 2: Auto-Create Collection if Missing"]
    B["Step 2: Auto-Create Collection if Missing"] --> C["Step 3: Inject 12-Byte _id ObjectId & Write BSON"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 3. Document Ingestion Mechanics (CRUD Create) > Single Document Insertion (insertOne())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What is the exact syntax of `insertMany()` for batch-inserting multiple student documents in a single call?
cards.back: Passing `db.students.insertMany([{ name: "Meera", age: 17 }, { name: "Kabir", age: 18 }])` transmits the entire array in one network roundtrip.
cards.key_takeaway: Batching documents in an array with insertMany minimizes network roundtrip overhead during bulk ingestion.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Array Payload [{doc1}, {doc2}]"] --> B["db.students.insertMany([...])"]
    B["db.students.insertMany([...])"] --> C["Single Roundtrip Batch Write"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 3. Document Ingestion Mechanics (CRUD Create) > Batch Document Ingestion (insertMany())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In cursor-based querying, how does the return value of `db.students.find({ age: 18 })` enable pipeline modifier chaining?
cards.back: Because `find()` returns a lazy `Cursor` object rather than a static document, callers can chain `.sort()`, `.skip()`, and `.limit()` onto the cursor before streaming results.
cards.key_takeaway: Cursor objects returned by find allow modifier chaining before streaming results to the client.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Step 1: Call db.students.find({ age: 18 })"] --> B["Step 2: Receive Lazy Cursor Object"]
    B["Step 2: Receive Lazy Cursor Object"] --> C["Step 3: Chain .sort(), .skip(), .limit()"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read) > Cursor-Based Querying (find())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: True or False — You can chain `.sort({ age: -1 })` or `.limit(5)` directly onto `db.students.findOne()`? Explain why.
cards.back: **False.** Because `findOne()` immediately resolves to a single BSON document object (or `null`) instead of a `Cursor`, calling `.sort()` or `.limit()` on it fails.
cards.key_takeaway: The findOne method returns a resolved document object or null, so cursor methods cannot be chained on it.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    W["❌ Misconception: findOne() supports .sort() and .limit() chaining"] --> R["✅ Reality: findOne() returns a document or null, not a Cursor"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read) > Single Document Lookup (findOne())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the Query Operators table, how do comparison operators (`$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$ne`) and array operators (`$in`, `$nin`) nest inside a filter?
cards.back: Comparison and array membership operators are placed inside a field's value object, such as `db.students.find({ age: { $gte: 18 } })` or `db.students.find({ age: { $in: [17, 18, 19] } })`.
cards.key_takeaway: Comparison and array membership operators nest inside the target field's filter value object.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Field Key { age: ... }"] --> B["Comparison: { $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $ne }"]
    A["Field Key { age: ... }"] --> C["Array Membership: { $in: [...], $nin: [...] }"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination > Conditional Filter Operators

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In `db.students.find({}, { name: 1, age: 1, _id: 0 })`, what is the role of the `_id: 0` key in the second argument?
cards.back: Because `_id` is included by default in every projection, specifying `_id: 0` explicitly suppresses the primary key so only `name` and `age` are returned.
cards.key_takeaway: Always include _id: 0 explicitly in your projection when you want to omit the primary key from results.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Projection { name: 1, age: 1, _id: 0 }"] --> B["1 Includes name and age"]
    B["1 Includes name and age"] --> C["_id: 0 Suppresses Default Primary Key"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination > Field Projection Mechanics

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What is the exact execution order of cursor modifiers in `db.students.find().sort({ age: 1 }).skip(10).limit(5)`?
cards.back:
- `limit(n)` caps the number of documents returned; `skip(n)` omits the first n — commonly combined for pagination."

1. `sort({ age: 1 })` orders matching documents ascending.
2. `skip(10)` omits the first 10 results.
3. `limit(5)` returns the next 5 results.
cards.key_takeaway: Chaining sort, skip, and limit implements deterministic offset-based pagination over query results.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    S1["1. find() Matches Docs"] --> S2["2. sort({ age: 1 }) Orders Ascending"]
    S2["2. sort({ age: 1 }) Orders Ascending"] --> S3["3. skip(10) Omits First 10"]
    S3["3. skip(10) Omits First 10"] --> S4["4. limit(5) Emits Next 5"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination > Cursor Pipeline Transformation & Pagination

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How do you write `updateOne()` and `updateMany()` commands using `$set` to update Rahul's age to `20` and promote all 18-year-old students?
cards.back:
- `updateMany(filter, update)` applies the same update to every matching document."

Run `db.students.updateOne({ name: "Rahul" }, { $set: { age: 20 } })` for a single match and `db.students.updateMany({ age: 18 }, { $set: { promoted: true } })` for all matches.
cards.key_takeaway: Both updateOne and updateMany require an atomic operator like $set to modify fields in place.
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 6. Field Modification & In-Place Update Operators (CRUD Update) > Update Scope & Execution Methods

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How are `$set`, `$inc`, and `$push` combined inside a single `db.students.updateOne()` call to mutate multiple fields atomically?
cards.back: Pass `{ $set: { age: 20 }, $inc: { attempts: 1 }, $push: { subjects: "History" } }` as the second argument to `db.students.updateOne({ name: "Rahul" }, ...)` to apply all three mutations atomically.
cards.key_takeaway: A single updateOne call can combine $set, $inc, and $push to mutate multiple scalar and array fields atomically.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Filter: { name: 'Rahul' }"] --> B["Update Object: { $set, $inc, $push }"]
    B["Update Object: { $set, $inc, $push }"] --> C["Atomic In-Place Multi-Field Mutation"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 6. Field Modification & In-Place Update Operators (CRUD Update) > Atomic Field Update Operators

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })` differ from `db.students.deleteMany({ age: 17 })` when multiple documents match?
cards.back:
- `deleteMany(filter)` deletes every matching document."

`deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })` removes strictly the first matching `"Kabir"` record and leaves duplicates untouched, whereas `deleteMany({ age: 17 })` deletes every document with `age: 17`.
cards.key_takeaway: Use deleteOne when removing a single record and deleteMany when purging all records matching a criterion.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Multi-Match Deletion Behavior"] --> A["deleteOne: Stops after deleting first match"]
    D["Multi-Match Deletion Behavior"] --> B["deleteMany: Deletes every matching document"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 7. Document Deletion & Collection Pruning (CRUD Delete) > Document Deletion Execution Methods

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `db.students.deleteMany({})` differ from `db.students.drop()` in terms of collection container and index survival?
cards.back: `db.students.deleteMany({})` deletes all documents while preserving the `students` collection container and its indexes, whereas `db.students.drop()` permanently destroys the container, documents, and indexes.
cards.key_takeaway: Passing an empty filter to deleteMany removes all documents while preserving the collection container and its indexes.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Container & Index Survival"] --> A["deleteMany({}): Keeps collection container & indexes"]
    D["Container & Index Survival"] --> B["drop(): Destroys collection container & indexes"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 7. Document Deletion & Collection Pruning (CRUD Delete) > Data Cleanup Architectural Tradeoffs

cards.front: Which three default system databases are displayed by `show dbs` on a freshly initialized MongoDB server?
cards.back: As shown in the reference slide output (`admin 0.000GB`, `config 0.000GB`, `local 0.000GB`), every MongoDB server includes the `admin`, `config`, and `local` system databases by default alongside populated user databases.
cards.key_takeaway: Every MongoDB server includes the admin, config, and local system databases by default.
